referents.why: 'say to him' (3ms) is Moses's commanded speech; the one he is told to speak to is Pharaoh, the one the go-command sends him to.
'my people' in the words Yahweh says ('thus he says Yahweh'); the first person of that speech is its speaker, w14.
referents.category: first person inside a divine speech

referents.why: 'serve me' in the same speech; the first person is the speaker, Yahweh.
referents.category: first person inside a divine speech

referents.why: implied 'you' of the command 'go', spoken by Yahweh to Moses (w4), the one he speaks to in cl0.
implied 'you' of 'you will say to him' (2ms): still Moses, the one commanded.
implied 'you' of 'let my people go' inside Yahweh's message, which is addressed to Pharaoh (w7).
referents.category: implied subject inside a quoted command

referents.why: 'that they may serve me' is third plural; the people (w17) is the collective whose going is commanded.
referents.category: third person plural after a command

links.why: a clause linked to itself; the narrative frame of the speech has no second event.
a command followed by a weqatal continuing the same speech ('go ... and you will say to him').
waw joins a command to a third-person yiqtol; that is a purpose, not a plain and.
command then waw + yiqtol in a different person: 'let them go, so that they may worship Me'.
the saying clause introduces the commands it reports (R1).
'say to him' introduces Moses's message, which is Yahweh's words (R1).
'thus he says Yahweh' introduces the imperative group of the message (R1).

groups.why: outer speech of Yahweh to Moses; its parts are the two commands and the commanded speech to Pharaoh (R2).
two commands joined by waw at one level are one imperative group.
Moses's words to Pharaoh, the commanded turn; its sender is the one commanded to speak (R2).
innermost turn: Yahweh's words quoted by Moses; sender is the one quoted (R2).
the command 'let my people go' with its aim (so that they may worship); the waw clause is an aim, not a part.
